correctness.rationale: The SIS generator Poisson equations on each nonempty infected subset have off-diagonal infection rate lambda*d_S(v), recovery rate1, and reward |S|; the absorbing empty state gives a unique positive finite expectation. Coupling with shared recovery/infection clocks proves burden strictly increases on adding an edge for uniformly seeded infections. Deleting any vertex from n<=4 leaves <=3 vertices, for which each possible residual edge count corresponds to a nested graph isomorphism type, hence maximum-degree vaccination is optimal uniformly in lambda. For the n=5 graph edges {01,02,04,12,13,23}, deletion 0 gives K3+K1, deletion 1/2 gives P4, and other deletions have strictly larger burden. Independent exact 15-state rational Poisson solves reproduce B_K3+K1=(3lambda²+3lambda+2)/2 and the displayed degree-eight rational B_P4. Their signed difference has numerator lambda²(lambda+1)(48lambda^5+136lambda^4+99lambda^3-78lambda²-156lambda-72), with positive denominator. Descartes sign variation and endpoint signs prove exactly one positive root, bracketed numerically at 1.0282979668; optimum switches {1,2} to {0} with tie {0,1,2}. This proves the claim for all positive rates, not just tested samples.
residual_risks: No claim for n>5 or vaccination choices beyond exactly one perfectly removed vertex.

originality.rationale: Earlier graph vaccination switches in Reed–Frost bond-percolation/SIR models concern final outbreak size, while SIS survival studies typically concern extinction time or initial infected-set rankings. The finite-graph intervention objective here is integrated infected person-time, including reinfections. No inspected earlier theorem yields the present all-rate cutoff and unique algebraic crossover.
residual_risks: Earlier finite-state SIS intervention calculations may exist under integrated prevalence or network occupancy terminology.
Experimental interpretation depends on the stipulated objective and homogeneous rates, not biological vaccine efficacy.

value.rationale: Exact order-four universality and the first order-five rate-dependent vaccination reversal establish a sharp decision-theoretic boundary on a natural stochastic network model. The crossover compares a connected corridor with a dense core plus isolate under time-integrated prevalence, a quantity not interchangeable with SIR final size or SIS extinction time. Unique algebraic threshold and complete optimizer sets are independently useful finite structural facts.
residual_risks: No policy claim for empirical vaccination or heterogeneous networks.

limitations: Exactly one perfectly vaccinated vertex, uniformly random initial infected person among survivors, one-unit recovery, no imports, cumulative person-time loss.
